title: Per-route/model/customer cost & latency heatmap indexer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a backend component that ingests streaming inference telemetry and materializes compact, queryable heatmap indices representing joint cost and latency distributions across three primary dimensions: route, model variant, and customer (tenant). The indexer will produce pre-aggregated tiles for the Console UI and APIs so customers can explore per-route and per-model cost/latency patterns by percentile and sequence-length buckets without scanning raw events.
motivation: Current Console queries against raw rollups are slow and expensive for multi-dimensional slices (route x model x customer x seq_length). Product needs fast, interactive heatmap views to (1) surface anomalous routes that drive unit-cost regressions, (2) let customers correlate latency vs cost across model variants, and (3) power alerting/quality baselines for rollouts.
goals: 1) Produce a daily and hourly heatmap index for top N routes and on-demand for cold routes. 2) Keep index storage under 5% of existing rollup volume via sparse tiling + compression. 3) Provide query latency <200ms for top routes and <1s for ad-hoc tenant queries. 4) Quantile error <=2% for p50/p95/p99 estimations.
non_goals: Per-request raw trace retention, full-fidelity token-level traces in the index, or replacing the canonical billing pipeline. This is a complementary fast view layer.
approach_summary: Streaming ingestion from Kafka -> Flink (stream processor) for online incremental tiles + Beam batch job for backfill and compaction. Use t-digest per tile for quantiles, reservoir sampling for extreme tail preservation, and sparse matrix tiles keyed by (route_id, model_family, tenant_id, seq_bucket, time_bucket). Store tiles in ClickHouse for fast point reads and in S3 as compressed Parquet for longer-term backfill/repairs. Expose an HTTP indexer API for Console to fetch tile slices.
data_model_notes: Tile key format: route:<route_id>|model:<model_sha_or_family>|tenant:<tenant_id>|time:<YYYY-MM-DDTHH>|seq_bucket:<0-12>. Each tile stores: count, token_count, t-digest(serialized base64), top_k_config_variants(list), cpu_gpu_seconds_estimate, compressed_kv_cache_hit_rate_est. Tiles are sparse and sharded by route hash to balance hot routes.
algorithm_tradeoffs: We chose t-digest for compact quantile estimation (good for p50/p95/p99) at the expense of exact medians for tiny samples. Reservoir sampling retains tail-outliers but increases state for extremely high-throughput routes; mitigated by adaptive sampling cap per-tenant. Storing both an online ClickHouse hot-store and S3 cold-store makes queries fast but requires compaction jobs to avoid divergence.
infra_impact: Flink job + ClickHouse retention increase estimated ~3 dedicated streaming workers and a ClickHouse shard increase (2 vnodes). S3 cost for Parquet tiles is expected to be ~1.8% of current telemetry storage. Will require autoscaling rules for spikes and improved schema registry coordination.
api_contracts: GET /v1/insights/heatmap?route_id={}&model_family={}&tenant_id={}&start={}&end={}&resolution=hour|day returns JSON with grid metadata and base64 t-digest per cell. Accepts optional seq_bucket filter. Auth via existing Console token with tenant-scoped view.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hourly index produced for top-500 routes within 10 minutes of window close.
- Query latency <200ms 95th for top routes in ClickHouse.
- Quantile estimates within 2% of full-scan t-digest baseline for synthetic workloads.
- End-to-end tests covering ingestion->tile materialization->API.
- Console team integration demo completed and UX signoff.
- Monitoring: per-job lag, tile-drop rate, index size delta should be visible in grafana dashboards.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype t-digest tile emitter in a feature branch and run against 7 days of replay (DEV cluster). 2) Implement Flink streaming operator to maintain per-tile state and emit checkpoints. 3) ClickHouse schema and API server for tile reads. 4) Beam batch compaction job to reconcile S3 and ClickHouse tiles. 5) Add E2E tests and dashboarding. 6) Canary deploy for 50 routes, validate correctness and perf, then expand to top-500.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Hot routes explode state and slow Flink operator. Mitigation: route sharding + adaptive sampling + separate hot-path path that emits coarse tiles only.
Risk: T-digest divergence after compaction. Mitigation: deterministic merge tests and daily verification job.
Risk: ClickHouse cost. Mitigation: aggressive TTLs for non-top routes and move older tiles to S3.
work_log: 2026-02-22: Spike: ran 7-day replay with a t-digest tile prototype against dev telemetry; observed p95 error ~1.4% for ample samples. Saved prototype results: gs://redwood-dev/heatmap-spike/

2026-02-25: Design review with Console UX. Accepted tile size suggestion of 12 seq_length buckets x 5 percentile bands. Action: add seq_bucket cardinality to tile key. Notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/HEATMAP-INDEXER

2026-03-02: Architecture sync with infra. Decided on ClickHouse hot-store + S3 cold-store, Flink for online; infra to allocate 3 streaming workers initially. PR opened for schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-platform/pull/12345

2026-03-06: Implemented reservoir sampling cap per-route (default 10k samples/min). Ran load test; memory stable for top-200 routes. See load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/heatmap-loadtests
2026-03-09: PM feedback: prioritize tenant-scoped heatmaps in initial canary. Updated plan to canary 50 tenant-route pairs first.
